page: Google Cloud Platform m2-ultramem-416 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for workloads requiring massive memory footprints. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 416 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors running at 2.7 GHz, corresponding to 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 11,776 GB of system memory, providing approximately 28.31 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%, indicating limited performance for single-threaded tasks. However, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 20,571.16 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 296.37 GB/sec. Conversely, the Passmark memory score is relatively weak, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is rated poor.

Given its hardware profile, the m2-ultramem-416 is highly cost-efficient for specialized, large-scale in-memory database deployments, such as SAP HANA, where resource density and massive memory capacity outweigh single-thread CPU speed. It is also well-suited for high-throughput Redis deployments, achieving 324.46 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, and high-volume static web serving. It is less suitable for tasks dependent on high single-core clock speeds, local NVMe storage, or GPU-accelerated machine learning training.
